newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Police open fire to prevent Indonesia jailbreak.
newsitem.headline: Police open fire to prevent Indonesia jailbreak.

text.p: Police fired warning shots and teargas to prevent inmates from escaping after a fire broke out in a prison in Indonesia's East Java province, official media reported on Thursday.

The official Antara news agency said the fire broke out in the Maedang prison late on Wednesday near the provincial capital Surabaya, but none of the 610 inmates, who included three activists accused of subversion, escaped.
The activists from the unrecognised People's Democratic Party, Mochamad Soleh, Dita Indah Sari and Coen Husein Pontoh, were sentenced for subversion in April, said Antara.
Antara quoted East Java police spokesman Lieutenant-Colonel Sofwat Hadi as saying 25 people were being questioned for alleged involvement in the fire.
"The investigation is not finished yet. Police are trying hard to reveal the cause of the fire," he said.
Antara gave no further details, but said police barricaded the prison during the blaze and fired warning shots and teargas to prevent inmates from escaping.

The Suara Pembaruan evening newspaper quoted prison officials as saying the fire was started by inmates. It said a number of inmates whose cells were damaged by the fire had been transferred to other prisons.
